exposure: Thromboembolism type (deep vein thrombosis vs. pulmonary embolism)
cohort: 6,269,641 women hospitalized for delivery in the United States from January 1 to October 31 in 2013 and 2014
finding: The majority of postpartum venous thromboembolism readmissions occurred within 20 days of discharge, and several risk factors were identified, including history of venous thromboembolism, cesarean delivery, thrombophilia, longer delivery hospitalization, and preeclampsia or gestational hypertension.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was associated with increased odds of postpartum venous thromboembolism readmission (odds ratio, 2.0; 95% confidence interval, 1.8-2.3).
